correctness.rationale: For weight-three supports translation always aligns one point, and aligning two is equivalent to a shared undirected separation. Thus, outside a single rotation class, distances are 2 if the profiles meet and 4 otherwise. Consecutive gap bounds give the explicit centres through 11; parity gives centres at 12 and 14. At 13 the allowed signed differences form a symmetric set A of size at least 6; |A+A|≥11 by Cauchy–Davenport, so (A+A) meets A and the allowed graph contains a triangle. For n≥15 at most 3n edges are excluded, so Mantel forces a triangle and hence a distance-four adversary for every centre. At 14 the triangle-free equality case must be K_{7,7}; translation by one swaps its bipartition classes, since otherwise transitivity is impossible. Hence the forbidden separations are precisely 2,4,6. After halving on one parity class, the gaps have distinct absolute separations 1,2,3 and sum to seven, so they are 1,2,4. Their two cyclic orders give the two indicated rotation orbits; x↦2−x interchanges the representatives, but rotation preserves gap order up to cyclic shift. Burnside gives the total number in the radius-four regime, since the only nonidentity stabilizing rotations have order three. The finite census independently checks the additional multiplicities.

reproduction.evidence: An independent exact census of n=3,…,14 canonicalizes by actual rotations and minimizes 6−2|T∩(U+s)| over all shifts, without using separation profiles. The optimal-centre counts are 1,1,2,4,5,7,6,10,10,2,22,2; at 14 precisely (0,2,6) and (0,2,10) among 26 orbits. This corroborates only those lengths; the infinite result uses the analytic bound. value.rationale: Weight three is a natural fixed-content layer for cyclic Hamming geometry. The result completely resolves its one-centre radius over all lengths and locates a nonmonotone exception at exactly fourteen, identifying its two reversal-related but rotation-distinct centres. The relation between this exceptional length and equality in the triangle-free extremal bound is structural, not just a finite census.
